from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, main-20261015: coherent finite-level mapping-complex adjunction before R lim. Supporting the graph adjunction in fixed-object enriched rectification: Corollary A.5.4 and Lemma A.5.5, printed pp. 93-94; Theorem A.5.3 provides the pointwise functor-category calculation.

proof.text: Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the cocartesian fibration of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], writing the base for its nerve. The algebra definition in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] identifies algebras with the full subcategory of $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal M,\mathcal V^\otimes)$ on inert-preserving functors. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-section-colimits] with $T=\mathcal M$, $g$ its structure map, and $K=\Delta^0$. Its hypotheses hold: $\Delta^0$ is small and weakly contractible; the identity cocone is a one-object colimit in every fiber, and every transport preserves these colimits. Indeed the mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies a colimiting one-object cocone with an equivalence edge. The section theorem therefore says that a transformation in $\mathcal F$ is an equivalence exactly when each component is an equivalence in its fiber.

source.place: Lemma A.5.5, with the singleton case of Theorem A.5.3 and the target Segal equivalences.

proof.text: For $x\in\mathcal M_{[n]}$, choose the inert projections $e_i:x\to c_i$ supplied by [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. For an algebra map $f:A\to A\prime$, its naturality square along $e_i$ has cocartesian horizontal edges, because algebras preserve inert edges. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-transport-square] with base arrow $\rho_i$, $R=A(e_i)$, $T=A\prime(e_i)$, $u=f_x$ and $v=f_{c_i}$. Its comparison identifies $\rho_{i,!}(f_x)$ with $f_{c_i}$ after conjugating by the displayed equivalences. The Segal equivalence in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] is induced by these transports. Thus if all color components are equivalences, every coordinate of $f_x$ is an equivalence, so $f_x$ is an equivalence: take the inverses and their two triangle witnesses coordinatewise. For $n=0$ the fiber is equivalent to the terminal empty product, so its edges are equivalences as well. Step 1 now makes $f$ an equivalence in $\mathcal F$ and in the full algebra subcategory (the inverse and its triangle witnesses remain there). Conversely evaluation sends an inverse and its witnesses to an inverse and its witnesses. This proves conservativity of $U_{\mathcal M}$.

source.place: Lemma A.5.5, with the singleton case of Theorem A.5.3 and the target Segal equivalences.

proof.text: Fix a small sifted $K$. By [lem-coef-infinity-sifted-colimit-calculus], it is weakly contractible. Presentability in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and presentable monoidality in [def-coef-complete-algebroid] give all small colimits in $\mathcal V$ and their separate preservation by tensor. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], the fibers $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal V^n$ have $K$-colimits coordinatewise. Apply the bifunctor clause of the sifted-calculus lemma to tensor: it preserves simultaneous $K$-colimits. Inducting on $r\geq1$, the $r$-fold tensor does too: the case $r=1$ is the identity. For $r+1$, first apply $(X_1,\ldots,X_{r+1})\mapsto(X_1\otimes\cdots\otimes X_r,X_{r+1})$. The induction hypothesis and the pointwise product-colimit criterion show that this functor preserves the given colimit cocone in $\mathcal V^2$. Binary tensor then preserves it by the bifunctor clause. To identify this composite with the $(r+1)$-fold tensor, factor the active map $[r+1]\to[1]$ of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ as $\psi:[r+1]\to[2]$, opposite to $0\mapsto0$, $1\mapsto r$, $2\mapsto r+1$, followed by the active map $[2]\to[1]$. By the transport-composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] the $(r+1)$-fold tensor is binary tensor after $\psi_!$, and by the block formula of step 4 (whose verification does not use this step) $\psi_!$ has coordinates $X_1\otimes\cdots\otimes X_r$ and $X_{r+1}$. For $r=0$ the operation is constant at $\mathbf1$; the weak-contractibility clause of [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula] says the identity constant cocone is colimiting.

source.place: Lemma A.5.1; HTT Proposition 5.5.8.6 for tensor and Corollary 4.4.4.9 for empty blocks.

proof.text: For $\phi:[n]\to[m]$ opposite to $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, the $j$th coordinate of $\phi_!$ tensors the block $X_{\theta(j-1)+1},\ldots,X_{\theta(j)}$; an empty block gives $\mathbf1$, and coordinates outside these blocks are discarded. To verify the block formula, factor $\rho_j\phi$ as the inert map $[n]\to[r]$ opposite to $a\mapsto\theta(j-1)+a$, followed by the active map $[r]\to[1]$, where $r=\theta(j)-\theta(j-1)$. The first transport selects the block and the second tensors it, by [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]; composition of transports is supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with diagram shape $\Delta^0$. Step 3 shows that every block preserves $K$-colimits, including its nullary case, so every transport $\phi_!$ preserves $K$-colimits. The product-colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] then applies to its output coordinates, including the terminal fiber at $[0]$.

source.place: Lemma A.5.1; HTT Proposition 5.5.8.6 for tensor and Corollary 4.4.4.9 for empty blocks.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-section-colimits] to $p$, $g:\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, this $K$, and the specified set of inert edges of $\mathcal M$. Steps 3-4 verify exactly its fiber-existence and transport-preservation hypotheses. It gives a colimit $L$ of $B$ in $\mathcal F$, computed in each fiber. Its closure clause implies that $L$ sends every inert edge to a cocartesian edge, so $L$ is an algebra by [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. The ambient colimit cocone is also colimiting in the full algebra subcategory: for any algebra $C$, fullness identifies both its mapping space from $L$ and its mapping spaces from $B_k$ with the ambient ones, so the same colimit mapping-space equivalence applies. At a color $c$, the section theorem evaluates this actual cocone to a colimit in $\mathcal V$. Thus $L(c)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_k B_k(c)$ with its canonical cocone. The pointwise functor-category clause of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] now identifies $U_{\mathcal M}L$ with the colimit of $U_{\mathcal M}B$.

source.place: Corollary A.5.4 (i)-(iii), obtained from Theorem A.5.3, and the algebra part of (iv).

proof.text: For any algebra cocone $B\Rightarrow A$, the colimit cocone $B\Rightarrow L$ of step 5 gives a comparison $q:L\to A$ compatible with the cocones. If the cocone to $A$ is colimiting at every color, then $q(c)$ is an equivalence because both its source and target cocones are colimits of the same color diagram. Step 2 makes $q$ an equivalence of algebras; hence the cocone to $A$ is colimiting. Conversely, if it is colimiting, $q$ is an equivalence of algebras and step 5 makes every color cocone colimiting. This proves detection, and step 5 already proves preservation.

source.place: Corollary A.5.4 (iv)-(v), restricted to algebra cocones; comparison with the constructed colimit.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-sifted-colimit-calculus], $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted in the required infinity-categorical sense. Substitute it for $K$ in steps 3-6. Thus every geometric realization exists, its color at $c$ is $\operatorname{colim}_{[n]\in\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}B_n(c)$, and its colimit cocones are detected at every color.

title: Colorwise detection of equivalences and sifted colimits of operadic algebras
statement:
Use the universes and monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the generalized nonsymmetric operads and their algebras of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad, and let $\mathcal V$ be a presentably monoidal infinity-category. Write $U_{\mathcal M}:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M_{[1]},\mathcal V)$ for restriction to colors. A morphism of $\mathcal M$-algebras is an equivalence if and only if its value at every color is an equivalence. Let $K$ be any small sifted infinity-category, meaning that $K$-indexed colimits of spaces commute with finite products. For every diagram $B:K\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ its colimit exists and is computed on each color $c$ by
$$ (\operatorname*{colim}_{k\in K}B_k)(c)\simeq\operatorname*{colim}_{k\in K}B_k(c). $$
A cocone of algebras is a colimit cocone if and only if it is one at every color. Thus $U_{\mathcal M}$ preserves and detects small sifted colimits. These assertions apply in particular to geometric realizations, indexed by $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$.
